title: Frame frontmatter (Markdown serialization)
description: Schema for the YAML frontmatter of a Frame written in the reference serialization: a Markdown artifact whose metadata is a YAML mapping between '---' delimiters. Validate the parsed frontmatter mapping against this schema. The Markdown body is not covered here: it is free-form text and the spec places no structural requirement on it. Extension fields are permitted.

type.$comment: Required. The self-identifying hook. Exactly 'frame', or 'frame [<major>.<minor>]'. The bracketed token names the spec conformance family; patch-qualified tokens such as 'frame [0.2.0]' are not valid.

name.$comment: Required. Short human-readable name for the Frame.

description.$comment: Required. One or two sentences on what the Frame is for and when it should be used.

visibility.$comment: Required. Not a closed set: the spec suggests these four values but does not restrict the field to them, so this is 'examples' rather than 'enum'.

version.$comment: Recommended. The Frame's own revision, not the spec version. The spec does not mandate a versioning scheme, so no pattern is enforced.

scope.$comment: Recommended. Where the Frame applies. The spec defines no formal scope grammar.

maintainer.$comment: Recommended. Person, team, or organization that maintains the Frame.

inherits.$comment: Recommended. One parent Frame as a string, or several as a list. Earlier entries have lower precedence than later ones; the child always wins. Values are references an implementation can resolve, typically a path, name, or URI.
